item.text:
**7B.6 Research Note**
Mostly no, with narrow institutional pushback.

**Accepted items**
- **PM Modi declares total assets worth Rs 3.02 crore in poll affidavit** | The Economic Times / Reuters | 14 May 2024 | https://m.economictimes.com/news/elections/lok-sabha/india/pm-modi-declares-total-assets-worth-rs-3-02-crore-in-poll-affidavit/amp_articleshow/110119535.cms | Claim: Modi’s mandatory election affidavit publicly disclosed assets, income sources, and lack of pending criminal cases, which is weak positive evidence for transparency around his own assets. | IDs: 7B.6; 7B.4
- **India’s Supreme Court puts on hold unit for fact-checking online content about govt** | Reuters via ThePrint | 21 Mar 2024 | https://theprint.in/india/india-top-court-puts-on-hold-unit-for-fact-checking-online-content-about-govt/2009612/ | Claim: The government tried to create a fact-checking unit with powers to label content about government business false or misleading, but the Supreme Court stayed it, showing an attempt to control scrutiny of official claims rather than tolerate it. | IDs: 7B.6
- **India top court puts on hold unit for fact-checking online content about govt** | Reuters via ThePrint | 21 Mar 2024 | https://theprint.in/india/india-top-court-puts-on-hold-unit-for-fact-checking-online-content-about-govt/2009612/ | Claim: The Court’s stay is also weak positive evidence that an independent institution could still block censorship-like government moves in 2024. | IDs: 7B.6
- **India’s election panel seeks responses from Modi, Rahul Gandhi** | Reuters via ThePrint | 25 Apr 2024 | https://theprint.in/india/indias-poll-panel-seeks-responses-to-complaints-against-modi-rahul-gandhi/2056144/ | Claim: The Election Commission formally processed complaints about Modi’s campaign rhetoric, indicating that independent election oversight still operated and could demand a response from the incumbent. | IDs: 7B.6
- **Indian vote body tells X to remove Modi party video targeting Muslims, opposition** | Reuters via ThePrint | 7 May 2024 | https://theprint.in/india/indian-vote-body-tells-x-to-remove-modi-party-video-targeting-muslims-opposition/2074462/ | Claim: The Election Commission ordered a takedown of a BJP campaign video and the government did not override the order, which is modest evidence of tolerating independent electoral enforcement. | IDs: 7B.6
- **India’s poll panel orders Modi’s BJP, opposition Congress to show restraint in campaign** | Reuters via ThePrint | 22 May 2024 | https://theprint.in/india/indias-poll-panel-orders-modis-bjp-opposition-congress-to-show-restraint-in-campaign/2096809/ | Claim: The Election Commission found the parties’ defenses “not tenable” and issued notices, another sign that outside scrutiny of Modi’s campaign behavior remained active. | IDs: 7B.6
- **Explainer: What were India’s electoral bonds and how did they power Modi’s party?** | Reuters via ThePrint | 16 Feb 2024 | https://theprint.in/india/explainer-what-were-indias-electoral-bonds-and-how-did-they-power-modis-party/1969006/ | Claim: India’s Supreme Court struck down the anonymous-donation system that had benefited the BJP, which is evidence that scrutiny of campaign finance could still reach Modi-era structures. | IDs: 7B.6; 7B.4
- **Modi’s party distances itself from India’s Adani amid opposition protests** | Reuters via ThePrint | 26 Nov 2024 | https://theprint.in/india/modis-party-distances-itself-from-indias-adani-amid-opposition-protests/2375102/ | Claim: After Adani’s U.S. indictment, opposition parties accused Modi’s government of shielding him and demanded parliamentary probe action, showing that scrutiny of a politically connected ally was publicly contested but not obviously shut down. | IDs: 7B.6; 7B.4

**Negative items**
- **India: Laws Misused to Crack Down on Peaceful Dissent** | Human Rights Watch | 8 Feb 2024 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/02/08/india-laws-misused-crack-down-peaceful-dissent | Claim: HRW says the BJP-led government used FCRA pressure, raids, and politically motivated investigations against civil society groups, which is direct evidence against tolerance of independent scrutiny. | IDs: 7B.6
- **India: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report** | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/india/freedom-world/2024 | Claim: Freedom House reports that attacks on press freedom escalated under Modi, journalists face harassment, and investigations do occur but under a worsening climate, which is strong background evidence against tolerant scrutiny. | IDs: 7B.6
- **India | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism** | Reuters Institute | 17 Jun 2024 | https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/india | Claim: The report says new laws, broad regulatory powers, and the NewsClick raids created a chilling effect on press freedom and scrutiny of the government. | IDs: 7B.6
- **Inside Modi’s crackdown on the foreign press in India** | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 13 Nov 2024 | https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/news/inside-modis-crackdown-foreign-press-india | Claim: India denied renewals and work permits to foreign correspondents critical of the government, which is strong evidence against tolerance of independent investigation. | IDs: 7B.6
- **India’s election panel tells X to remove Modi party video targeting Muslims, opposition** | Reuters via ThePrint | 7 May 2024 | https://theprint.in/india/indian-vote-body-tells-x-to-remove-modi-party-video-targeting-muslims-opposition/2074462/ | Claim: The BJP used campaign material that triggered formal electoral intervention, suggesting the governing party was not self-restraining in ways compatible with open scrutiny. | IDs: 7B.6
- **India poll watchdog’s inaction lets PM Modi commit “brazen” violations, opposition says** | Reuters via ThePrint | 11 May 2024 | https://theprint.in/india/india-poll-watchdogs-inaction-lets-pm-modi-commit-brazen-violations-opposition-says/2080067/ | Claim: Opposition parties said the Election Commission was not meaningfully penalizing Modi’s violations, which undercuts any claim of a robustly tolerated independent check. | IDs: 7B.6
- **Indian opposition calls for Adani probe, Modi’s BJP questions timing of US indictment** | Reuters via ThePrint | 21 Nov 2024 | https://theprint.in/india/indian-opposition-calls-for-adani-probe-modis-bjp-questions-timing-of-us-indictment/2367046/ | Claim: Opposition allegations that Modi’s government protected Adani show persistent suspicion around scrutiny of a close business ally, even if the article itself does not prove a cover-up. | IDs: 7B.6; 7B.4
- **Modi’s party distances itself from India’s Adani amid opposition protests** | Reuters via ThePrint | 26 Nov 2024 | https://theprint.in/india/modis-party-distances-itself-from-indias-adani-amid-opposition-protests/2375102/ | Claim: The article frames the Adani affair as an explicit test of whether Modi’s ecosystem would permit independent examination of a politically connected conglomerate. | IDs: 7B.6; 7B.4

**Bottom line**
- There is some evidence of formal oversight still functioning in 2024, especially the Election Commission and Supreme Court.
- The stronger pattern is negative: pressure on civil society, press, and information channels; attempts to create a government fact-checking unit; and persistent allegations around opaque finance and Adani.
- Search gap: I did not find a clean 2024 source showing Modi personally welcomed independent investigations into his own conduct or assets. The best evidence is indirect and institutional, not a direct statement of tolerance.
